claim: Amazon API Gateway implements the token bucket algorithm according to account and Region limits and can be configured per client with usage plans; SQS and Kinesis can buffer requests, and AWS WAF can rate-limit specific API consumers that generate unusually high load.

values.display: implements the token bucket algorithm according to account and region limits
configured per-client with usage plans

evidence.quote: Amazon API Gateway implements the token bucket algorithm according to account and region limits and can be configured per-client with usage plans. Additionally, Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) and Amazon Kinesis can buffer requests to smooth out the request rate, and allow higher throttling rates for requests that can be addressed. Finally, you can implement rate limiting with AWS WAF to throttle specific API consumers that generate unusually high load.

claim: You can configure API Gateway with throttling limits that return 429 Too Many Requests errors when limits are exceeded, use AWS WAF with API Gateway endpoints for rate limiting on a per IP address basis, and put messages into a queue or stream where asynchronous processing is tolerable to burst to higher throttle rates.

values.display: return `429 Too Many Requests` errors when limits are exceeded
rate limiting on a per IP address basis

evidence.quote: You can configure API Gateway with throttling limits for your APIs and return `429 Too Many Requests` errors when limits are exceeded. You can use AWS WAF with your AWS AppSync and API Gateway endpoints to enable rate limiting on a per IP address basis. Additionally, where your system can tolerate asynchronous processing, you can put messages into a queue or stream to speed up responses to service clients, which allows you to burst to higher throttle rates.
